senses.gloss: वैशद्य n. (fr. वि-शद) clearness, purity, brightness, freshness (with मनसि, ‘cheerfulness of mind’), Suśr.; VarBṛS.; Sarvad.
distinctness, intelligibleness, Sāy.
whiteness, MW.
वैषद्य w.r. for वैशद्य.
वैशन्त॑ mf(ई)n. (fr. वेशन्त) contained in or forming a tank, RV.; VS.; TS.; Br.
belonging to a Soma ladle or cup, MW.
वैशन्त॑ n. a cup of Soma juice, MW.
वैशन्ता॑ (आ॑), f. = वे॑शन्ता, a tank, VS.

वैशम्पायन m. (patr. fr. विशम्-प) N. of an ancient sage (teacher of the Taittirīya-saṃhitā [q.v.]; in epic poetry a pupil of Vyāsa and also the narrator of the Mahā-bhārata to Janam-ejaya), GṛS.; TĀr. &c. (cf. IW. 371 n. 1)
of an author, Cat.
of a son of Śuka-nāsa (transformed into a parrot), Kād.
वैशम्पायन—नीति-संग्रह m. N. of wk.
वैशम्पायन—संहिता f. N. of wk.
वैशम्पायन—स्मृति f. N. of wk.
वैशम्पायनीय mfn. of or belonging to Vaiśampāyana, Cat.
वैशम्फल्या (ĀpŚr.) or वैशम्बल्या (ib.) or वैशम्भल्या॑ (TBr.) f. N. of Sarasvatī.
वैशली f. N. of a wife of Vasudeva, VP. (v.l. वैशाली)
of a town, MW. (cf. वि-शला, वैशाली).
वैशाली f. a daughter of the king of Viśālā, MBh.
N. of a wife of Vasudeva, VP. (v.l. वैशली)
of a town founded by Viśāla, R.; Pur.; Buddh.
वैशालि m. patr. of Su-śarman, MārkP.
वैशल्य n. (fr. वि-शल्य) deliverance from a painful encumbrance (as that of the fetus), Car.
वैशस mfn. (fr. a form वि-शस, derived fr. वि-√ शस्; cf. वि-शसन) causing death or destruction, MBh.
वैशस n. (ifc. f(आ). ) rending in pieces, MW.
वैशस n. slaughter, butchery, war, strife, injury, hurt, outrage, distress, calamity, ruin (with प्रेम्णः, ruin of affection), MBh.; Hariv.; Kāv. &c.
the hell, BhP.
N. of a hell, ib.
वैशस्त्य n. (fr. वि-शस्ति), Gaṇar.
1. वैशस्त्र mfn. (fr. वि-शसितृ [विशस्तृ]), Pāṇ. iv, 4, 49, Vārtt. 2
वैशस्त्र n. government, sway, rule, W.
2. वैशस्त्र n. (fr. वि-शस्त्र) the state of being unarmed, L.
वैशस्य n. an abstr. noun fr. विशसि, g. ब्राह्मनादि (Kāś.)
w.r. for वैषम्य, Kathās.
वैशाख॑ m. (fr. वि-शाखा) one of the 12 months constituting the Hindū lunar year (answering to April-May and in some places, with Caitra, reckoned as beginning the year), ŚBr.; Lāṭy.; MBh. &c.
a churning-stick, Śiś. xi, 8
the seventh year in the 12 years' cycle of Jupiter, VarBṛS.
वैशाख॑ n. a partic. attitude in shooting, Hariv.
N. of a town (also -पुर), Kathās.
वैशाख॑ mf(ई)n. relating to the month Vaiśākha, ŚāṅkhGṛ.
वैशाखा (आ), f. N. of a lioness, Cat.
वैशाखी (ई), f. (with or scil. पौर्णमासी) the day of full moon in the month Vaiśākha, GṛŚrS.; MBh. &c.
a kind of red-flowering Punarnavā, L.
N. of a wife of Vasu-deva, Hariv.; VP.
वैशाख—पुराण n. N. of wk.
वैशाख—मास-व्रत n. N. of wk.
वैशाख—माहात्म्य n. N. of wk.
वैशाख—रज्जु f. the string on a churning-stick, L.
वैशाख—वदि ind. in the dark half of the month Vaiś˚, Inscr. (in giving dates).
वैशाखिन् m. a partic. part of an elephant's forefoot, L.
वैशाख्य m. N. of a Muni, Cat.
वैशाय्य n. (fr. वि-शाय), Gaṇar.
वैषय n. (fr. वि-षय) = विषयाणां समूहः, g. भिक्षादि.
वैशारद mf(ई)n. (fr. वि-शारद) experienced, skilled, expert, unerring, BhP.
वैशारद n. profound learning, R.
वैशारद्य n. experience, skill in (loc.), expertness, wisdom, MBh.; Bālar.; Sāh.
clearness of intellect, infallibility, Yogas.; BṛĀrUp., Sch.
Buddha's confidence in himself (of four kinds), Divyāv. (cf. Dharmas. 77).
वैशाल mfn. descended from Viśāla, BhP.
वैशाल m. N. of a Muni, Cat.
वैशालक mfn. relating to or ruling over Vaiśālī, VP.
वैशालाक्ष n. N. of the Śāstra composed by Śiva as Viśālākṣa, MBh.
वैशालायन m. patr. fr. विशाल, g. अश्वादि.
वैशालिक mfn. relating to Viśālā (Vaiśālī), R.
वैशालिनी f. patr. fr. विशाल, MārkP.
वैशालीय mfn. (fr. विशाल) g. कृशाश्वादि.
वैशालेय॑ m. patr. of Takṣaka and of other serpent-demons, AV.; ŚāṅkhGṛ. &c.
वैशिक mf(ई)n. (fr. 1. वेश) relating to or treating of prostitution, Mṛcch.
associating with courtezans, versed in the arts of courtezans, L.
वैशिक n. harlotry, the arts of harlots, R.; VarBṛS.; Gaut.; Buddh.
वैशिक्य m. pl. N. of a people, MārkP.
वैशिख mfn. (fr. वि-शिखा) g. छत्त्रादि.
वैशिष्ट n. (fr. वि-शिष्ट) distinction, difference (= next), Sāh. (prob. w.r.)
वैशिष्ट्य n. endowment with some distinguishing property or attribute, distinction, peculiarity, difference, Caṇḍ.; Tarkas.; Sāh. &c.
pre-eminence, excellence, superiority, MBh.; Kām. &c.
वैशीति m. patr. fr. विशीत, g. तौल्वल्य्-आदि.
वैशी-पुत्र॑ m. (वैशी = वैश्या + प्˚) the son of a Vaiśya woman, Br.
वैशेय m. patr. fr. विश, g. शुभ्रादि.
वैशेषिक mf(ई)n. (fr. वि-शेष, p. 990) special, peculiar, specific, characteristic, Āpast.; Suśr.; Bhāṣāp.; Hcat.
distinguished, excellent, pre-eminent, MBh.
relating or belonging to or based on or dealing with the Vaiśeṣika doctrine, Bhāṣāp.; Madhus.
वैशेषिक m. a follower of the V˚ doctrine, Kap.; Kusum.; Buddh.
वैशेषिक n. peculiarity, distinction, Kaṇ.

N. of the later of the two great divisions of the Nyāya school of philosophy (it was founded by Kaṇāda, and differs from the ‘Nyāya proper’ founded by Gautama, in propounding only seven categories or topics instead of sixteen; and more especially in its doctrine of विशेष, or eternally distinct nature of the nine substances, air, fire, water, earth, mind, ether, time, space, and soul, of which the first five, including mind, are held to be atomic), IW. 65 &c.
वैशेषिक—दर्शन n. N. of wk.
वैशेषिक—रत्न-माला f. N. of wk.

वैशेषिक—सूत्र n. the aphorisms of the Vaiśeṣika (branch of the Nyāya philosophy, which have been commented on by a triple set of commentaries, and expounded in various works, of which the best known are the Bhāṣā-pariccheda with its commentary, called Siddhānta-muktāvalī, and the Tarkasaṃgraha), IW. 60 n. 1
वैशेषिक—सू˚त्रोपस्कर n. N. of wk.
वैशेषिकादि-षड्-दर्शन-विशेष-वर्णन n. ‘description of the difference between the Vaiśeṣika and other systems’, N. of a phil. wk.
वैशेषिन् mfn. specific, individual, Sāṃkhyak., Sch.
वैशेष्य n. peculiarity, specific or generic distinction, TPrāt.; Suśr.; Vedāntas.
difference, superiority, pre-eminence, Mn. ix, 296 &c.
वैश्मिक mfn. (fr. वेश्मन्) living in a house, Car.
वैश्मीय mfn. (fr. id.) g. कृशाश्वादि.
वै॑श्य m. (fr. 2. विश्) ‘a man who settles on the soil’, a peasant, or ‘working man’, agriculturist, man of the third class or caste (whose business was trade as well as agriculture), RV. &c. &c.
pl. N. of a people, VarBṛS.
वै॑श्य n. vassalage, dependance, TS.
वै॑श्य mfn. belonging to a man of the third caste, MBh.
वै॑श्या (आ), f. See below
वैश्या f. a woman of the Vaiśya caste, Mn.; Yājñ. &c.
N. of a deity, Buddh.
वैश्य—कन्या f. a Vaiśya damsel, a girl of the agricultural class, Mn. x, 8.
वैश्य—कर्मन् n. the business of a Vaiśya, agriculture, trade (˚म-पुस्तक n. N. of wk.)
वैश्य—कर्म-पुस्तक n. N. of wk.
वैश्य—कुल n. the house of a V˚, KātyŚr.
वैश्य—घ्न m. the slayer of a V˚, VarBṛS.
वैश्य—चरित्र n. N. of wk.
वैश्य—जातीय m. a V˚ (by birth), man of the third caste, L.
वैश्य—ता f. the state or condition of a V˚ (acc. with √ गम्, to become a V˚), AitBr.; MBh. &c.
वैश्य—त्व n. = -ता, MārkP.
वैश्य—ध्वंसिन् mfn. destroying V˚, VarBṛS.
वैश्य—पुत्र m. the son of a Vaiśya, a Vaiśya, Siṃhās.
वैश्या—पुत्र m. ‘son of a Vaiśya mother’, N. of Yuyutsu, MBh.
वैश्य—पुर n. N. of a town, Vīrac.
वैश्य—भद्रा f. N. of a deity, Buddh.
वैश्य—भाव m. = -ता, Mn. x, 93.
वैश्य—यज्ञ m. the sacrifice performed by a V˚, KātyŚr.
वैश्य—योनि f. a V˚'s mode of existence, ChUp.
वैश्य—रत mfn. living at the expense of the Vaiśyas, Cat.
वैश्य—वृत्ति f. a V˚'s mode of life or occupation, agriculture, trade, Mn. x, 83.
वैश्य—सव m. a partic. sacrificial rite, TBr.
वैश्य—स्तोम m. N. of an Ekāha, ṢaḍvBr.; ŚrS.
वैश्यान्तर m. N. of Buddha in his last birth but one, MWB. 113.
वैश्या—ज mfn. born of a Vaiśya woman, the child of a Vaiśya mother, Mn. ix, 151.
वैश्रमण w.r. for वैश्रवण.
वैश्रम्भक mfn. (fr. वि-श्रम्भ) awakening or inspiring confidence, BhP.
वैश्रम्भक n. N. of a celestial grove, ib.
वैश्रवण॑ m. (fr. वि-श्रवण; cf. g. शिवादि) a patr. (esp. of Kubera and Rāvaṇa), AV. &c. &c.
(in astron.) N. of the 14th Muhūrta
वैश्रवण॑ mf(ई)n. relating or belonging to Kubera, MBh.
वैश्रवणानुज m. ‘younger brother of K˚’, N. of Rāvaṇa, R.
वैश्रवणालय m. ‘K˚'s abode’, the Indian fig-tree, L.
N. of a place, Cat.
वैश्रवणावास and वैश्रवणोदय, m. ‘Kubera's glory’, the Indian fig-tree, L.
वैश्रवणावास and वैश्रवणोदय, m. ‘Kubera's glory’, the Indian fig-tree, L.
वैश्रेय m. patr. fr. विश्रि, g. गृष्ट्यादि.
वैस्रेय m. patr. fr. विस्रि, g. शुभ्रादि.
वैश्लेषिक mf(ई)n. (fr. वि-श्लेष), Cat.
वैश्व mf(ई)n. (fr. विश्व, of which it is also the Vṛddhi form in comp.), relating to or presided over by the Viśve Devāḥ
वैश्व n. id., VarBṛS.

वैश्वी f. N. of the Nakṣatra Uttarāṣāḍhā, L.
वैश्व—कथिक mfn. (fr. विश्व-कथा) g. कथादि.

a partic. Ekāha, ŚāṅkhŚr.
वैश्वदेव॑ n. a partic. Śastra, AitBr.
the first Parvan of the Cāturmāsya, TBr.; ŚBr.

(exceptionally m.) N. of a partic. religious ceremony which ought to be performed morning and evening and especially before the midday meal (it consists in homage paid to the Viśve Devāḥ followed by the बलि-हरण or offering of small portions of cooked food to all the gods who give the food and especially to the god of fire who cooks the food and bears the offering to heaven), Āpast.; Mn. &c. (cf. RTL. 417)
N. of partic. verses or formulas, TBr.; ŚBr.
of various Sāmans, ĀrṣBr.
the Nakṣatra Uttarāṣāḍhā (cf. under वैश्व), VarBṛS.

a kind of metre, Śrutab.

corresponding to the V˚-d˚ ceremony, Yājñ.

the fire of digestion, MW.
the sun, sunlight, AV.; ŚāṅkhBr.
(in the Vedānta) N. of the Supreme Spirit or Intellect when located in a supposed collective aggregate of gross bodies (= Virāj, Prajā-pati, Puruṣa), Vedāntas, RTL. 35
N. of a Daitya, Hariv.; Pur.
of various men, Kathās.
(pl.) of a family of Ṛṣis, MBh.
वैश्वानर॑ n. men collectively, mankind, TBr.
N. of a Sāman, ĀrṣBr.
